I need a channel beam with 70mm width, 40mm height, a length 450mm with a wall thickness of 5mm, which is open on the top side | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (description only)

1. Choose an orientation  
   • X-axis = flange-to-flange width (70 mm).  
   • Y-axis = beam length (450 mm).  
   • Z-axis = section height (40 mm, bottom→top).  
   The global origin (0, 0, 0) will be the bottom-left-front corner of the channel’s outer envelope.

2. Create the full outer volume of the beam  
   • Call functions.block once with subtraction = False.  
   • Use x_size = 70, y_size = 450, z_size = 40.  
   • Basepoint (x,y,z) = (0, 0, 0).

3. Hollow the interior while leaving 5 mm thick walls and keeping the top side completely open  
   • Call functions.block a second time with subtraction = True.  
   • Offset the inner block by the wall thickness from each closed face:
     – x = 5 mm, y = 5 mm, z = 5 mm.  
   • Dimensions of inner block:
     – x_size = 70 − 2·5 = 60 mm  (5 mm side walls)  
     – y_size = 450 − 2·5 = 440 mm (5 mm walls at both beam ends)  
     – z_size = 40 − 5 = 35 mm   (5 mm bottom wall, top remains open because the inner block reaches z = 40)

4. After both block calls, invoke functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled = True).

Result: a channel beam 70 mm × 40 mm in cross-section, 450 mm long, with 5 mm-thick bottom and side walls and an open top surface, spatially aligned so every inner face is exactly 5 mm from its corresponding outer face.
